Simulated compositions from a Dirichlet distribution

Source: R/tph.R
dirsim.Rd

Compositions that are closed (each row sums to total) and positive, such as the element shares a portable X-ray fluorescence scan reports, drawn from the Dirichlet distribution with concentrations alpha: each part is a gamma variate of shape alpha[j] and rate 1 divided by the sum of its row. Normal noise is the wrong model for such data, as it leaves the simplex. The draws are for testing a compositional analysis before real measurements exist (clrilr(), tpbhm()), never a substitute for them. The mean share of part j is alpha[j] / sum(alpha); larger concentrations give less spread around it.

Usage

dirsim(n, alpha, total = 1, seed = NULL)

Arguments

n

The number of compositions: a whole number from 1 to 2147483647.

alpha

The concentration of each part: positive finite numbers, at least two; their names name the columns.

total

What each composition sums to: one positive number (1 for shares, 1e6 for parts per million).

seed

NULL to draw the seed from R's generator, or one whole number from 0.

Value

A numeric matrix of n rows and one column per part.

Details

The gammas are drawn part by part, n of each, from R's generator (Mersenne-Twister with inversion, as set.seed() seeds it), so that set.seed(seed); g <- matrix(rgamma(n * k, rep(alpha, each = n)), n) gives the same draws and g / rowSums(g) * total the same result. Without seed one is drawn from R's generator.

References

Aitchison, J. (1986). The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and Hall. doi:10.1007/978-94-009-4109-0

Examples

# a calcium-rich profile and a natural one, in parts per million
lime <- c(Ca = 85, P = 5, Fe = 2, Sr = 0.5, Pb = 0.2, Zn = 0.2)
soil <- c(Ca = 30, P = 15, Fe = 5, Sr = 1, Pb = 0.5, Zn = 0.5)
x <- rbind(dirsim(5, lime, 1e6, seed = 1), dirsim(5, soil, 1e6, seed = 2))
round(x)
#>           Ca      P     Fe    Sr   Pb    Zn
#>  [1,] 916028  64989   9709  8530  338   406
#>  [2,] 924519  59016  10998  3742 1585   139
#>  [3,] 926699  55681  13866     7  343  3403
#>  [4,] 948999  41626   6514    75    0  2786
#>  [5,] 918903  38403  34643  7958   93     0
#>  [6,] 545725 298947  82563 67504 1473  3788
#>  [7,] 656421 315410  24984   307 2854    24
#>  [8,] 490101 333923 148857 25907   52  1160
#>  [9,] 549398 336330  94906  4794  858 13714
#> [10,] 553314 280049  72463 29418 2497 62259
clrilr(x)[, "Ca"]
#>  [1] 4.582492 4.644030 5.378437 6.646381 6.411516 2.577556 4.556793 3.286704
#>  [9] 2.856785 2.205577
